name: identify-uncertain-v1
purpose: Visibility Phase 2, Slice J1-Identify. A deterministic, self-contained arrangement that produces a genuinely UNCERTAIN Vault Browse card (VaultIdentifier::recordAmbiguous, identityState=='ambiguous' -> browseAt() row state=='uncertain') so an isolated Lanista session can drive the real in-place identify affordance on the rebuilt Browse face (Vault Browse Slice 6, landed 2026-08-13) and prove the card settles to 'identified' WITHOUT a grid rebuild, paired with one F1 vault-forensics scope=identity response for the same node.
provenance: Authored fresh for J1-Identify (2026-08-14). The 'Masterpiece' single-comic-folder trick is NOT invented here -- it is the exact mechanism the Vault Browse execution plan's own Slice 6 already proved live (tests/lanista_scenarios/vault_browse_uncertain.json, run against tests/fixtures/vault/browse-states-smoke-seed, comment dated 2026-08-13: 'the Masterpiece/ fixture folder's cleaned title has exactly TWO exact matches in the production offline comics catalogue (gcd_id 206859 and 218321)'). This fixture reuses the SAME real bundled catalogue fact (data/comics_catalog.db is the app's one production comics catalogue, not a per-fixture stub) inside its OWN self-contained fixture tree so J1-Identify never touches the Vault Browse plan's fixture (tests/fixtures/vault/browse-states-smoke-seed is out of this slice's fence). Independently re-verified against data/comics_catalog.db immediately before authoring this fixture: 'select gcd_id,title,year,publisher from series where lower(title)=lower(?)' for 'Masterpiece' returns exactly 2 rows (gcd_id 206859 'Masterpiece' 2023 Dark Horse; gcd_id 218321 'Masterpiece' 2024 Dark Horse) and for 'Akira' returns exactly 1 row (gcd_id 3636 'Akira' 1988 Marvel) -- not accepted on the prior agent's word alone, re-derived by direct query.
mechanism: VaultIdentifier::matchGroup() for kind=='comic' runs ComicsCatalog::exactMatches(cleanedFolderTitle) (case-insensitive exact title match against the real bundled data/comics_catalog.db) during the progressive per-event-loop-turn auto-identify pass (VaultLibrary::runAutoIdentifySlice). candidateCount==1 auto-adopts (VaultIdentifier::applyGroup -> identityState='adopted' -> browse row state='identified'). candidateCount>1 declines adoption and calls VaultIdentifier::recordAmbiguous() (identityState='ambiguous' -> browse row state='uncertain', native/engine/VaultLibrary.cpp lines ~646/755). A single-file comic folder named exactly 'Masterpiece' (no year/release tags to strip -- VaultKit::cleanMediaFolderTitle passes it through unchanged) deterministically lands on the candidateCount==2 branch every run; a folder named exactly 'Akira' deterministically lands on the candidateCount==1 auto-adopt branch every run. Neither depends on network access or a live catalogue lookup -- both catalogues (ComicsCatalog/MAL) are offline SQLite data bundled with the app.
confirmedRoot: media/ (this fixture directory) -- vault/config.json points a confirmed root directly at the absolute path of this fixture's own media/ subtree, exactly as tests/fixtures/vault/browse-face-smoke-seed and tests/lanista_fixtures/journeys/vault-browse-five-shapes-v1/vault/config.json already do. VaultLibrary::republishAtBoot() scans+publishes this root automatically at boot; no pre-built index is seeded. The progressive auto-identify pass (one group per event-loop turn) then settles the single group to 'uncertain' on its own -- the scenario waits for that settling, it never forces it.

negativeControl.purpose: Slice J1-Identify's mandatory negative control: prove the 'uncertain' wait is a real gate, not a vacuous pass, by pointing the SAME wait at a card that deterministically never becomes uncertain (candidateCount==1, auto-adopts instead).

placement.note: not auto-applied by the harness's generic placement walk -- driven as its OWN separate --seed root (this fixture directory's negative-control/ subtree), a fully self-contained nested vault+media pair, for the negative-control session run only.

negativeControl.confirmedRoot: negative-control/media/ -- negative-control/vault/config.json points a confirmed root at this fixture's own negative-control/media/ subtree.
negativeControl.howRun: Run the isolated session with --seed pointed at this fixture directory's negative-control/ subtree instead of the fixture root, then repeat ONLY the 'wait card state==uncertain' step (targeting the Akira card's own key) with a short bounded timeout -- it must time out/never match, proving the wait cannot pass vacuously. Restore by re-running the ordinary --seed against the fixture root (Masterpiece, ambiguous) and confirming green again.

note: Card cbz files are minimal 502-byte valid ZIP archives (three tiny 1x1 PNG entries: 001.png/002.png/003.png), generated fresh for this fixture -- mirrors the exact shape of the proven tests/fixtures/vault/browse-states-smoke/Masterpiece/Masterpiece.cbz and Akira/Akira.cbz fixtures (archive validity only matters for VaultScanner's file classification; auto-identify keys off the FOLDER name, never archive contents).
